chunks: Al-Fadl, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abul Jarud, from Muhammad ibn Bashir, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, who said:

I said to him: This matter has been prolonged, so when? He moved his head and then said: How can it be so, while the time has not yet 'bitten' (become harsh)? How can it be so, while the brothers have not yet dried up (ceased to be united)? How can it be so, while the ruler has not yet become oppressive? How can it be so, while the Atheist has not risen from Qazwin, tearing down its veils, exposing its insides, changing its walls, and removing its joy? Whoever flees from him, he catches him; whoever fights him, he kills him; whoever withdraws from him, he becomes poor; whoever follows him, he becomes a disbeliever; until two mourners arise: one who mourns for his religion and one who mourns for his world.

key_terms.الزَّمَانُ: The time/era, referring to the period of waiting
key_terms.الزَّنْدِيقُ: The Atheist or Doubter, a specific eschatological figure
key_terms.قَزْوِينَ: Qazwin, a city in Iran identified as the origin of the figure

ai.seo_question: What are the four signs preceding the reappearance of Imam Mahdi according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the 'Atheist' (al-Zanadiq) from Qazwin as a pivotal eschatological figure whose pervasive influence creates a universal dilemma of exile, war, or poverty, ultimately leading to widespread apostasy. The text underscores the spiritual crisis preceding the Imam's reappearance, where even those who follow him are consumed by disbelief, culminating in the emergence of the two 'weepers' (Bakiyan) who mourn both the loss of faith and worldly decline.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 433 - It is narrated from Fadhl from Ibn Abi Najran from Muhammad bin Sinan from Abul Jarud from Muhammad bin Bashar that he asked Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah about the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s) and he said:

“How is it possible so soon? The cruel time has not yet arrived. How is it possible so soon? As yet brothers have not started oppressing brothers. How is it possible so soon? The ruler of the time has not started oppressing. How is it possible so soon? The atheists have not staged an uprising from Qazwin. That they may halt their progress; who may change their town shelters, who destroys their joys, who apprehends those who try to flee from them, who kills those who come out to fight them, those who recede to solitude become needful, one who obeys them becomes a denier; so much so that there will finally be two kinds of mourners: One who will mourn for their religion and another, who will mourn for their world.”
